title: popover: expect a way to watch all "`toggle`" events even in shadow DOM on `window`
body:
### Background
I'm writing web-extensions, and I want to show a UI on the top of all webpage elements, so I used to add `z-index: INT32_MAX`.

When a page use `[popover]` to show an element in `#top-layer`, my UI is behind its `backdrop` and then may be invisible or blurred.

Then I did a test, and found if only I add `[popover=manual]` to my UI, then `UI.showPopover()` will make it top again

### Problem
I want to add `[popover=manual]` and call `showPopover` only when "necessary", so I need a way to know whether a page has used `popover` and activated a top layer.

But, currently the **`toggle` event is fired without specifying `composed`**, so a listener on `window` can not receive those inside Shadow DOM trees, which is described on https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#queue-a-popover-toggle-event-task and implemented as-is by Chrome 114.
 
### Potential solutions

1. simplest way: maybe we can add `composed=true` to `toggle` event
3. or, add a new member of `popoverElement: Element | null` to `HTMLDocument`, and then bind it to the front element in `#top-layer` if existing, or null when the `#top-layer` is empty
4. or, even add a complex member of `topLayerElements: NodeList<Element>` to `HTMLDocument`
- 1. then this list may even contain both `<* popover>` and `<dialog open>`

The 1st idea is simple and clear, while it means my extension need to listen `toggle` event, even a page never use the `popover` feature. I prefer not adding such listeners, so that my extension won't disturb webpage developers - when a developer add event breakpoints, the Dev Tools may pause in listeners of my extension >_<.

I haven't read the history of `<dialog>` standard, so I'm not sure whether the 4th idea has been aborted or not. Sorry for the duplication if any.
